findings.title: All 14 success criteria are covered — no gaps
findings.description:
Verified each criterion against the tasks:
- SC1 (StrEnum `OPEN/WRAP/REFLECT`) → Task 1.1
- SC2 (`policy` field, default `OPEN`) → Task 1.2
- SC3 (loader, case-insensitive, `ConfigError` on unknown) → Tasks 1.3 + 1.4
- SC4 (missing key → `OPEN`) → Tasks 1.3 + 1.4 (`test_bounds_policy_omitted_defaults_open`)
- SC5 (`config_to_yaml` round-trip) → Task 1.4 (`test_bounds_policy_yaml_round_trip`)
- SC6 (`OPEN` no-op, verified) → Task 2.3 (`test_open_is_noop_*`) + Task 3.4 (`test_open_policy_does_not_call_enforcement`)
- SC7 (WRAP into `[0,width)×[0,height)`, incl. negative + multi-width overshoot) → Task 2.3 WRAP tests
- SC8 (WRAP leaves velocities unchanged) → Task 2.3 `test_wrap_velocities_unchanged`
- SC9 (REFLECT clamp + flip outward velocity) → Task 2.3 REFLECT tests
- SC10 (`step()` calls after tick, not called on OPEN) → Tasks 3.2 + 3.4 (mock)
- SC11 (50+ tick integration, per-policy bounds) → Task 3.4 (`test_open_policy_allows_drift...`, `test_wrap_policy_keeps_all_positions_inside`, `test_reflect_policy_keeps_all_positions_inside`)
- SC12 (both shipped configs → `wrap`) → Tasks 4.1 + 4.2
- SC13 (full suite passes) → Tasks 3.5 + 5.1
- SC14 (manual viewer verification) → Task 5.2 (mirrors all 8 walkthrough steps)

No success criterion is left without a corresponding task.

findings.title: No scope creep — every task traces to the design
findings.description:
- Every implementation task traces to an in-scope item / success criterion.
- Task 3.3's startup INFO log line (`Bounds policy: wrap`) is not an SC on its own, but it is required by Verification Walkthrough step 4, so it is in scope.
- Tasks 5.3–5.5 (status updates, CHANGELOG entry, architecture check-off) are standard slice-completion bookkeeping, consistent with the slice's parent architecture list (line 43 shows the `(313)` item) and the project's commit conventions.
- None of the explicitly out-of-scope items (SOFT/ARENA force, mixed per-axis policies, per-profile policy, engine-integrator change, `WorldBounds.validate_positions`, distributed bounds) are touched; the Notes section even re-states the SOFT deferral. The repo's later `SOFT` variant comes from slice 314, not from 313's tasks.

findings.title: Sequencing, test-with pattern, commits, and proportionality are correct; no load-test/CI needed
findings.description:
- Dependencies respected, no cycles: Section 1 (config enum/field/loader) before Section 2 (enforcement module, which imports `BoundsPolicy`/`WorldBoundsConfig`) before Section 3 (integration, which needs both) before Section 4 (shipped defaults) before Section 5 (final verification).
- Test-with pattern followed in every section: 1.4 tests follow 1.1–1.3; 2.3 tests follow 2.1–2.2; 3.4 integration tests + 3.5 regression follow 3.1–3.3.
- Commit markers sit at working, tested points (1.5, 2.4, 3.6, 4.3) and a docs commit at the end (5.5) — neither after every task nor only at the very end.
- Proportional: 23 tasks across 5 sections for 14 criteria on a slice the design itself rates 2/5 effort — right-sized.
- The slice restates no numeric performance NFR (only "default path negligible," a design rationale), so no `tests/load/` task or CI load-gate is required. Not flagging their absence.

findings.title: Frontmatter is `status: complete` but every checkbox is still `[ ]`
findings.description: The frontmatter says `status: complete` (and the slice says the same, and the repo is fully implemented), yet every checkbox in the body remains unchecked. CLAUDE.md's Document Conventions say to check off completed tasks/subtasks. This is bookkeeping drift, not a plan defect, and does not block anything — worth a quick pass when the slice is closed out.

findings.title: Task 1.4 round-trip test asserts the policy field, not full `ServerConfig` equality
findings.description: SC 5 is worded as "reloading the emitted YAML produces an **equal `ServerConfig`**," but Task 1.4's `test_bounds_policy_yaml_round_trip` (as implemented in `tests/test_config.py#test_bounds_policy_yaml_round_trip`) only asserts the reloaded `policy == BoundsPolicy.WRAP`. The full-equality claim is still demonstrated in combination with the pre-existing `test_roundtrip_basic_config`, but that test runs with the default policy. Behavior is correct and the test passes, so this is informational only; tightening the assertion to a full `assert cfg2 == cfg` (or at least `world_bounds` equality with a non-default policy) would match SC 5's wording more literally.

findings.title: Tasks 4.1 and 4.2 are slightly granular
findings.description:
Each of Tasks 4.1 (`config/default.yaml`) and 4.2 (`config/test.yaml`) is "add one `policy: wrap` line and run a one-line `python -c` load check," followed by a shared commit in 4.3. These two micro-tasks could be merged into a single "update shipped config defaults" task. This is the only borderline over-division in the file and is not worth blocking on; each is independently verifiable, so keeping them separate is defensible.

One additional observation (not a finding): the plan (and the slice) specifies `world_bounds` as a **required** keyword on `SimulationManager.__init__` and directs updating every existing call site (Tasks 3.4/3.5), whereas the shipped `simulation.py` made it optional with a fallback to `entity_manager.world_bounds`. The plan is internally consistent and matches the slice's own "required keyword argument" wording, so this is a deviation at implementation time rather than a defect in the breakdown — no action needed on the plan itself.

structured_findings.summary: All 14 success criteria are covered — no gaps
No scope creep — every task traces to the design
Sequencing, test-with pattern, commits, and proportionality are correct; no load-test/CI needed
Frontmatter is `status: complete` but every checkbox is still `[ ]`
